notes.note: Checked the interruption window in the adapter conformance fixture. Untagged text is dropped while a cancelled prompt remains unresolved and resumed once only the successor owns output.
Checked the notification dispatcher with a settled Codex Stop followed by abort and cancelled completion. Only the Stop reaches notification scheduling.

Reviewed ACP prompt and mapper ownership. Message and reasoning updates require an attributable active turn. The mapper withholds them during cancelled-prompt settlement when the source may be ambiguous. Native steering, cancellation transport, and extension-error enrichment keep their documented contracts.

Reviewed the SDK turn ledger and callers. Stopped identity is bounded, and a named buffered reply or receipt cannot replace an active successor. Queue admission, provider follow-up markers and the result-settlement boundary retain their documented behavior.

Reviewed Codex terminal and output intake. The adapter distinguishes a completed Stop from ordinary native turn identification and drops late content and terminal publications for that stopped turn. It still reads the engine cursor when the settling turn owns it.

Reviewed the Codex interrupt RPC and terminal publication. The exact Stop is marked once before its abort is published. A later engine report cannot reset successor status or output. Concurrent send admission and provider configuration retain their documented behavior.
